policy.authorship: every instruction below is written for this project. US law protects a recipe's literary expression, not its ingredient list or its functional steps (37 CFR 202.1(a); Publications Int'l, Ltd. v. Meredith Corp., 88 F.3d 473 (7th Cir. 1996)); the instructions are written plainly and functionally on purpose, so no third-party prose is reproduced. The ten Kimatta entries and the owner's twenty-five household entries are ours end to end. The federal entries take only ingredient facts from the cited NHLBI publication, and each line retains the source's own quantity text in original_text so a conversion stays checkable (invariant 2).
policy.cook_review: cook_review is null until a human cooks the dish. Under D-041 the shipping rule is two-armed: an entry ships with a recorded cook_review OR with basis us_federal_public_domain and a source_url. The federal entries ship on the publisher arm. The owner's twenty-five household entries ship on the cook arm: 2026-09-06 is the date the owner attested that he or his wife has cooked each of them, not the date of a particular cooking, and each entry's cook_review.corrections says so. The ten Kimatta entries still need a cook and do not ship. See StarterRecipe::is_shippable.
policy.rights: basis us_federal_public_domain asserts: published by a US federal agency and asserted by that agency to be free of use restrictions. It is NOT a claim that 17 USC 105 operates automatically — 105 reaches works of federal officers and employees (101), and NHLBI states the Keep the Beat recipes were 'developed just for the NHLBI', i.e. contractor-developed. Shipping does not rest on the label: ingredient lists and functional steps are uncopyrightable and every instruction is rewritten. NHLBI asks that its material not be used in 'any direct or indirect product endorsement or advertising' and that the source be cited; rights.attribution carries that citation. MVP-020: render attribution, never the raw basis string, and never in a way that reads as NHLBI endorsing this app. Do not carry the sources' 'heart-healthy' framing into titles or copy — this app makes no health claim. Owner-approved 2026-09-05 at the MVP-032 Phase 0 stop.
policy.units: prefer the unit family a catalog id already carries, because UnitFamily::of puts tsp|tbsp|cup|fl_oz in VolumeUs, ml|l in VolumeMetric, g|kg in MassMetric, oz|lb in MassUs and piece in Count, and those families do not aggregate across each other -- so two lines on one id in different families become two shopping lines. Hence 8 oz reusing ing-spaghetti converts to g, and a half cup reusing ing-vegetable-broth converts to ml. This is a preference, not an invariant, and the file does not satisfy it everywhere: about eighteen ids carry two families because the recipes themselves measure differently -- '3 garlic cloves' against '1 Tbsp minced garlic', '1 lemon' against '2 Tbsp lemon juice', '2 carrots' against '1 C sliced carrots'. Forcing one family there would mean inventing a conversion the shopping module deliberately refuses to make (see shopping.rs: cross-system pairs are absent because 1 cup is not an exact number of ml). The split is the designed outcome: each line keeps its own original_text and stays separate. Nothing enforces the preference.
policy.expected_conflicts_note: expected_conflicts records what food_domain::assess actually returns under rule version 1, not a nutritional claim. peanut-noodle-bowl therefore declares gluten: rule version 1 matches the term "noodles" in "rice noodles", which are gluten-free. The declaration is kept honest rather than dodged by renaming the ingredient — MVP-009 accepted explainable false positives, over-warning is the safe direction, and the warning copy never claims safety. The reverse direction is present too and is the one to watch: rule version 1 has no gluten term matching soy sauce, so vegetable-fried-rice declares soy and sesame but no gluten conflict, even though conventionally brewed soy sauce is made with wheat and is a well-known hidden gluten source. peanut-noodle-bowl carries the same soy sauce and is flagged gluten only because "noodles" matches inside "rice noodles", so the roster is inconsistent on this one ingredient, and inconsistent in the unsafe direction on one of the two. Adding soy sauce to the gluten terms — and deciding the same question for tamari and miso, which rule version 1 already matches as soy but not as gluten — is an MVP-009 rule change with a RULE_VERSION bump, not a content edit; renaming the ingredient to dodge the matcher is not an option here either. One rule-version-1 miss arrives with the owner's household entries, in the unsafe direction and recorded rather than dodged: crockpot-barbecue-chicken and crockpot-chicken-tacos declare no dairy conflict for their ranch dressing and ranch seasoning lines, which are buttermilk-based; DAIRY's terms match neither "ranch dressing" nor "ranch seasoning". Adding "ranch" to the dairy terms is an MVP-009 rule change with a RULE_VERSION bump, not a content edit. A second miss was found and closed at the source instead: meatball-casserole declared no vegetarian conflict because MEAT_TERMS has no "meatball" or "meat" term and the line was named only "frozen meatballs". The owner confirmed 2026-09-06 that the meatballs are beef or turkey, so the ingredient is now named "beef or turkey meatballs" and the matcher sees the meat on both terms. That is an accuracy fix that happens to match, which is the opposite of renaming an ingredient to dodge a match -- the name got more true, not less. Where a name cannot be made more accurate, the miss stays declared, as the ranch lines above are.
policy.expected_conflicts_order: order is not significant: every_recipe_matches_its_declared_conflicts sorts both sides into RestrictionKind::ALL order before comparing, so entries may list expected_conflicts in any order.
policy.line_fidelity: one JSON line per source ingredient line, in source order, with original_text verbatim. Two deliberate exceptions, each also recorded in the entry's rights.modifications: a source that lists the same ingredient on two lines is merged and summed, and the two meatball sub-lists in turkey-and-beef-meatballs are flattened. Items the source marks optional, and garnishes, carry optional: true. Non-food equipment (skewers) is not a line; cooking spray is, because it is bought.
policy.prep_minutes: prep_minutes is the time the meal costs YOU, not its elapsed time. Tier 0 compares it against the household's SLOT_WINDOW policy, documented as 'Minutes available per slot', and a dish whose prep_minutes exceeds that window is REJECTED outright (tier0.rs, PREP_WINDOW_IMPOSSIBLE) rather than merely scored down. So the test when authoring is: could you leave the house while it cooks? Slow cooker yes, so record the active work only. Oven or stovetop no, so record prep plus cook. This is a workaround for the domain carrying one time field where it needs two (active and elapsed); see KNOWN_ISSUES.md and OPT-004. Owner decision 2026-09-06.
policy.pending_recipes: refs/recipes-pending.json holds five more of the owner's transcribed recipes that this file deliberately does not carry: three sides (honey glazed carrots, roasted green beans, roasted vegetables) and two breakfast or baking dishes (banana bread, apple cinnamon roll casserole). The planner covers dinner only and MealScope::dinner_only is still the default, and a side is not a meal, so shipping them today would make banana bread a candidate for Tuesday dinner. They are transcribed in the same shape as an entry here and need only a slot-suitability value. OPT-004 imports them; see its Phase 3.

recipes.title: Sheet-Pan Lemon Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.instructions: Heat the oven to 220C. Halve the potatoes and toss them with half the oil, the salt and the pepper on a sheet pan. Roast 15 minutes. Toss the chicken with the rest of the oil, the sliced garlic and the juice of the lemon. Add it to the pan and roast 25 minutes more, until the chicken reads 74C at its thickest point.

recipes.title: Red Lentil Soup
recipes.instructions: Soften the chopped onion and carrot in the oil over medium heat, about 8 minutes. Stir in the cumin for 30 seconds. Add the lentils and the broth, bring to a boil, then simmer 20 minutes until the lentils fall apart. Season with the salt and blend as smooth as you like it.

recipes.title: Black Bean Tacos
recipes.instructions: Cook the chopped onion in the oil over medium heat until soft. Add the cumin, then the drained beans and a splash of water, and mash about half of them. Simmer 5 minutes and season with the salt. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan and fill them. Finish with lime juice.

recipes.title: Creamy Tomato Spaghetti
recipes.instructions: Boil the spaghetti in salted water. Meanwhile melt the butter with the oil, cook the sliced garlic 1 minute, add the tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes. Stir in the cream and the salt. Drain the pasta, reserving a cup of its water, and toss it through the sauce, loosening with the water until it coats.

recipes.title: Peanut Noodle Bowl
recipes.instructions: Soak the rice noodles in hot water until pliable, then drain. Whisk the peanut butter with the soy sauce, the sesame oil, the juice of the lime and enough hot water to pour. Toss the noodles with the sauce, the julienned carrot and the sliced scallion.

recipes.title: Baked Salmon with Lemon Rice
recipes.instructions: Heat the oven to 200C. Rub the salmon with the oil and the salt and bake 12 minutes, until it flakes. Cook the rice in twice its volume of water. Fold the juice of the lemon and the chopped dill through the rice and serve the salmon on top.

recipes.title: Vegetable Fried Rice
recipes.instructions: Use rice cooked and cooled the day before. Scramble the beaten eggs in a hot pan and set them aside. Fry the diced carrot 3 minutes, add the peas, then the rice, breaking up the clumps. Return the eggs, add the soy sauce and the sesame oil, and finish with the sliced scallion.

lines.original_text: 3 cups white rice, cooked and cooled

recipes.title: Coconut Chickpea Curry
recipes.instructions: Soften the chopped onion in the oil, then cook the grated ginger and the sliced garlic 1 minute. Stir in the curry powder for 30 seconds, add the drained chickpeas and the coconut milk, and simmer 20 minutes until it thickens. Season with the salt.

recipes.title: Cheese and Black Bean Quesadillas
recipes.instructions: Mash the drained beans with the cumin. Spread them over half of each tortilla, scatter the grated cheddar over, and fold. Cook in a lightly oiled pan over medium heat, about 3 minutes a side, until the cheese has melted and the outside is crisp.

recipes.title: Garlic Shrimp Spaghetti
recipes.instructions: Boil the spaghetti in salted water. Cook the sliced garlic in the oil over low heat until it smells sweet, about 3 minutes. Raise the heat, add the shrimp and cook 3 minutes, until they are opaque throughout. Toss in the drained pasta with a splash of its water, the chopped parsley, the juice of the lemon and the salt.

recipes.title: Chicken Creole
recipes.instructions: Cut the chicken into thin strips. Heat a wide pan over medium-high heat and coat it lightly with oil. Cook the chicken until it is no longer pink, about 5 minutes. Add the tomatoes, chili sauce, pepper, celery, onion, garlic and herbs. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer 10 minutes, until the vegetables soften. Season with the salt and the crushed red pepper.

recipes.title: Steamed Salmon with Mushrooms and Ginger
recipes.instructions: Bring the broth to a simmer in a wide pan. Add the mushrooms, ginger and half the scallions and cook 2 minutes. Lay the salmon on top, cover, and steam 8 to 10 minutes, until the fish flakes at its thickest point. Lift the fish out, stir the soy sauce and sesame oil into the broth, and spoon it over. Scatter the rest of the scallions.

Stir the cornstarch into the lemon juice, add it with the sour cream, and cook 2 minutes until the sauce thickens. Season with the salt and pepper and scatter the herbs.

recipes.title: Barbecued Chicken
recipes.instructions: Heat the oven to 180C. Stir the tomato paste, ketchup, honey, molasses, worcestershire sauce, vinegar, cayenne, pepper, onion powder, ginger and garlic into a sauce. Set the chicken in a dish, brush it with half the sauce, and bake 1 hour, brushing with the rest twice, until it reads 74C at the thickest point.

recipes.title: Turkey and Beef Meatballs with Spaghetti
recipes.instructions: Heat the oven to 200C. Use both meats, or 340 g of either one alone. Mix the meat with the breadcrumbs, evaporated milk, cheese, chives and parsley and roll into 16 balls. Bake 20 minutes, until they read 74C. Boil the spaghetti until just tender and drain it. Warm the sauce, toss it with the pasta and the meatballs, and scatter the cheese and basil.
